claims.text: AIMD enhanced with machine-learned force fields can extend the accessible simulation times for HfNbTaTiZr.
Coupling AIMD and mode-resolved phonon Boltzmann transport will accurately separate lattice from electronic heat transport in defect-free HfNbTaTiZr.
The modeled material is defect-free, stoichiometric HfNbTaTiZr.
Machine-learned force fields will produce more accurate phonon-lifetime distributions than the earlier approaches.
Electronic transport can be computed separately using DFT-derived electronic scattering rates.
Atomic-mass and force-constant variations in HfNbTaTiZr influence phonon scattering.
AIMD captures anharmonic atomic motions in the disordered HfNbTaTiZr lattice.
Mode-specific phonon lifetimes can be extracted from the proposed AIMD calculations.
Feeding mode-specific phonon lifetimes into a Boltzmann transport framework permits computation of lattice thermal conductivity independently of electronic conductivity.
The lattice thermal conductivity of defect-free HfNbTaTiZr will decrease approximately as T^(-1), or more steeply, above 300 K.
The predicted lattice thermal conductivity will differ by approximately 20–30% from analytical estimates that mix lattice and electronic transport.
The electronic thermal-conductivity contribution of HfNbTaTiZr will remain nearly temperature-independent below 200 K.
Existing analytical approaches use averaged Debye temperatures and conflate lattice and electronic thermal transport.
The model is intended to operate from 50 K to 1200 K.
The predictions apply specifically to defect-free HfNbTaTiZr.
The approach may require modification for HfNbTaTiZr containing significant impurities such as oxygen.
Failure to observe the predicted 20–30% lattice-conductivity difference or the nearly constant sub-200 K electronic contribution would falsify the hypothesis.
